summary.name: PostOps: Recovery from Operations
summary.one_liner: A 2015 SREcon Europe talk by Todd Underwood of Google arguing for eliminating operations functions rather than just automating them.
use_cases: Learning the argument for eliminating ops work instead of automating it
Reading background on NoOps and SRE culture
Finding the updated version of the LISA13 PostOps talk
Reviewing ideas on software fragility and reliability
summary.what_it_does: ["This is a conference talk page, not a software tool. The talk is a shorter, updated version of the LISA13 talk 'PostOps: A Non Surgical Tale of Software, Fragility and Reliability'.", "It makes a call, similar to NoOps, for eliminating operations functions rather than simply automating them.", "The speaker is Todd Underwood, Site Reliability Director at Google, with earlier roles at Renesys and Oso Grande.", "The page includes a BibTeX citation (USENIX Association, Dublin, May 2015) and notes that USENIX posts slides and video for free after events."]
notable: Argues for eliminating operations functions rather than automating them
Updated, shorter version of the LISA13 talk
Presented at SREcon15 Europe in Dublin by a Google Site Reliability Director
caveats: Page text is a talk abstract only; no slides or video content is included in the text
